owned_invariants: A JSON number written as an optional minus and digits is read from those digits into an unbounded integer. A number written with a fraction or an exponent is kept as its text and is never an integer, whatever its value.

An object that has the same key twice is refused as BAD_JSON, at any depth, and so is nesting of lists and objects deeper than 64. Any other text that is not one JSON value is refused as BAD_JSON with the parser's position.

canonical writes one text per value: object keys in code point order, no white space, integers in decimal, decimals as they were written, and text with only the escapes JSON requires (quote, backslash, the five short escapes, and four lowercase hex digits for other control characters).
to_json keeps every integer exact: one that fits 64 bits goes out as a JSON number, a larger one and every decimal go out as text.
as_count gives a value only for an integer from zero up to the machine's usize.
boundaries: Syntax is delegated to serde_json with raw values; this module adds the duplicate-key, depth and exact-number rules on top of it.
A decimal is carried, never computed with. Exact arithmetic is in exact.rs and reads integers and p/q text only.
Text is compared by code point. No Unicode normalisation is applied to keys or values.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.
